title: The Erdős–Hajnal Theorems for the E-Graph and Bird

items.title: Deleting the middle pendant leaf of E gives the five-vertex path
items.statement: With the canonical labels, q has degree one in E and E-q is P_5. Hence the singleton family {E} is leaf-reducible.
items.proof_plan: Read all five edges: q is adjacent only to p_3, and deleting q leaves exactly p_1p_2,p_2p_3,p_3p_4,p_4p_5. Apply the published P_5 EH result and the singleton instance of leaf reducibility. No EH theorem for E is used.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path
Tung H. Nguyen, Notes on Recent Work on the Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture
references.locator: §1 pp.1–2, EH definition and the list of five-vertex prime graphs

items.title: The E-graph is generalized nice
items.statement: The finite singleton family {E} is generalized nice.
items.proof_plan: Use the already-published property-star corollary and the preceding leaf-reduction lemma as the two hypotheses of the property-star reduction. Retain the complement-family convention in the generalized-niceness definition.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path

items.title: The E-graph has the Erdős–Hajnal property
items.statement: There exists c_E>0 such that every nonempty finite simple induced-E-free graph G contains a clique or stable set with at least |V(G)|^{c_E} vertices.
items.proof_plan: The family {E} is finite, leaf-reducible by the first lemma, wonderful by the published wonderfulness lemma, and generalized nice by the preceding lemma. Instantiate the final reduction. It already converts the co-E-free intermediate formulation to E-free graphs; do not claim E-free equals co-E-free. This proof remains blocked by the upstream obligations in batch notes.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path

items.title: Deleting the extended horn leaf of Bird gives the bull
items.statement: With the canonical labels, w is a leaf of Bird and Bird-w is the bull. Hence {Bird} is leaf-reducible.
items.proof_plan: Check w is adjacent only to y. The remaining five edges are exactly the canonical bull edges. Apply the bull EH corollary, then the definition of leaf reducibility. Preserve the bull proof-closure blocker rather than treating its published status as proof.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path
Tung H. Nguyen, Notes on Recent Work on the Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture
references.locator: §1 pp.1–2, EH definition and the list of five-vertex prime graphs

items.title: The Bird family has property (*)
items.statement: The finite singleton family {Bird} has property (*).
items.proof_plan: Take H={Bird} and F_1=F_2={E}. Choose a common EH exponent c in (0,1] by downward closure from the earlier E theorem. For EVERY co-Bird-free graph and EVERY special-vertex comb in the property-star trigger, the co-Bird partition theorem supplies an E-free Y_i, a pure partition of X_i with E-free pattern, and vertexwise purity from every other B_h. These are exactly the local criterion clauses. Apply the special-vertex-local criterion, not the universally quantified all-combs criterion. Its constants may be c/4,10/c,c/4.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path
references.locator: Lemma 5.1 proof and Lemma 6.5; Theorem 1.10 used before 1.11

items.title: The Bird graph is generalized nice
items.statement: The singleton family {Bird} is generalized nice.
items.proof_plan: Apply the property-star reduction using the two preceding Bird interface lemmas. Wonderfulness is not a hypothesis of this intermediate reduction.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path

items.title: The Bird graph has the Erdős–Hajnal property
items.statement: There exists c_B>0 such that every nonempty finite simple induced-Bird-free graph G has a clique or stable set of size at least |V(G)|^{c_B}.
items.proof_plan: Instantiate the final reduction with the finite family {Bird}, its explicit leaf-reduction witness, published wonderfulness, and the preceding generalized-niceness lemma. The E theorem is already proved earlier and enters through property star; there is no reverse dependency. This proof remains blocked by the upstream obligations in batch notes.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path

items.title: The complements of E and Bird have the Erdős–Hajnal property
items.statement: The co-E-free and co-Bird-free classes have respectively the same admissible EH exponents as the E-free and Bird-free classes.
items.proof_plan: Apply complement invariance separately to the two established singleton results. This is a consequence, not a substitute for either headline theorem.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path

items.title: Dependency ledger for the final E and Bird deductions
items.statement: The E deduction precedes and supplies the auxiliary EH class in the Bird deduction. The two leaf deletions use P_5 and the bull respectively.
items.proof_plan: Give the exact local chain and source-label dictionary: 1.12=3.5; 1.13=4.5; 1.14=5.1 with the local special-vertex variant. Include the H_5/co-E auxiliary chain behind E property star. Do not restate a theorem as a new result or hide an unresolved supplier.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path

summary: The E-graph and Bird extend two established Erdős–Hajnal cases by one pendant vertex. Explicit leaf deletions identify the five-vertex path and bull, while the earlier wonderfulness and generalized-niceness reductions supply the remaining interfaces. The E theorem is deduced first from its co-E structural partition and the auxiliary H_5/co-E class.

The E theorem then supplies the auxiliary exponent for the special-vertex comb partitions in co-Bird-free graphs. This yields Bird’s property (*), generalized niceness, and Erdős–Hajnal theorem in that order. Complement consequences and a dependency ledger make the quantifiers, orientations, and proof order explicit.

title: The Erdős–Hajnal Theorems for the E-Graph and Bird — Examples

items.title: Edge tables for the two leaf deletions
items.statement: List the six-vertex edge sets of E and Bird, their complements, and the induced graphs after deleting q and w respectively.
items.proof_plan: List each of the 15 pairs exactly once; E has 5 edges and co-E 10; Bird has 6 and co-Bird 9. Delete q or w and compare each remaining pair against P_5 or bull.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path

items.title: Homogeneous numbers of E, Bird, and their complements
items.statement: For E, (alpha,omega)=(3,2); for Bird, (alpha,omega)=(3,3); the complements swap these numbers.
items.proof_plan: Exhibit stable sets and cliques and rule out larger ones from the full adjacency tables. For E, use the disjoint edges p_1p_2,p_3q,p_4p_5 to bound alpha by 3, and its bipartition to exclude triangles. For Bird use triangle {x_1,x_2,x_3}, stable set {x_3,z,w}, and the partition into the triangle and edges yw plus singleton z to bound alpha by 3; any clique using a pendant vertex has size <=2.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path

items.title: An E-free graph can contain an induced five-vertex path
items.statement: The implication E-free implies P_5-free is false.
items.proof_plan: Take G=P_5: it is E-free because it has only five vertices, but it contains itself as an induced P_5. This checks why extending the forbidden pattern enlarges the class and the new theorem is stronger.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path

items.title: A Bird-free graph can contain an induced bull
items.statement: The implication Bird-free implies bull-free is false.
items.proof_plan: The five-vertex bull is Bird-free by order, but not bull-free. Give its explicit five edges and the identity induced embedding.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path

items.title: Both types of homogeneous set are needed
items.statement: For every n>=1, K_n and its edgeless complement are both E-free and Bird-free. Their homogeneous numbers are n, realized by a clique and stable set respectively.
items.proof_plan: Every induced subgraph of a complete graph is complete, and of an edgeless graph is edgeless; both forbidden graphs have edges and nonedges. Compute (alpha,omega)=(1,n) and (n,1), including n=1. This illustrates the disjunctive conclusion and does not assign a numerical optimal EH exponent.

references.title: Huang, Ju and Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path
